question: Which of the following species is endemic to the Great Nicobar Island and not naturally found anywhere else in the world?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Nicobar Megapod**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Nicobar Megapod** (**Megapodius nicobariensis**) is a ground-dwelling bird that is **endemic** to the **Nicobar Islands** in the **Bay of Bengal**. It is not found naturally anywhere else in the world. ***Hence, the correct answer is Nicobar Megapod.***
 
• The **Lion-tailed Macaque** (**Macaca silenus**) is an **Old World monkey** endemic to the **Western Ghats** of **South India**. It is primarily found in the states of **Kerala**, **Karnataka**, and **Tamil Nadu**. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect.***
 
• The **Indian Pangolin** (**Manis crassicaudata**) is a **scaly anteater** found in various habitats across **India**, **Sri Lanka**, **Nepal**, and **Pakistan**. It is not restricted to a single island group. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect.***
 
• The **Great Hornbill** (**Buceros bicornis**) is a large bird found in the **Indian subcontinent** and **Southeast Asia**. Its range includes the **Western Ghats**, the **Himalayan foothills**, and countries like **Thailand** and **Indonesia**. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• The **Nicobar Megapod** belongs to the **Megapodiidae** family, whose members are known as **mound-builders**. These birds are unique because they do not sit on their eggs to provide warmth; instead, they build large **incubation mounds** of soil and **decaying vegetation**. The heat generated by the decomposition of organic matter incubates the eggs.
 
• The species is primarily found in **coastal forests** and **mangrove** areas. Its population is concentrated on islands like **Great Nicobar**, **Little Nicobar**, **Teressa**, and **Nancowry**. It is about the size of a **domestic hen** and has **brown plumage** with **large, strong feet**.
 
• It is currently listed as **Vulnerable** on the **IUCN Red List**. The **2004 Indian Ocean Tsunami** caused a severe decline in its population, as many of its nesting mounds were located on the **beaches** and were destroyed by the waves.
 
• In **India**, the species is protected under **Schedule I** of the **Wildlife Protection Act, 1972**, which provides it the highest level of legal protection against hunting and trade.
 
• The **Great Nicobar Biosphere Reserve** was established to protect the unique biodiversity of the island. It covers approximately **85%** of the island's area and was designated a **UNESCO Biosphere Reserve** in **2013**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Great Nicobar Island** is the largest and **southernmost** island of the **Nicobar** group. It is located about **190 kilometers** north of the **Indonesian** island of **Sumatra**.
 
• The island features a **tropical wet evergreen forest** ecosystem, which supports various endemic fauna, including the **Nicobar Tree Shrew**, **Nicobar Serpent Eagle**, and the **Nicobar Long-tailed Macaque**.
 
• **Indira Point**, located at **6 degrees 4 minutes North** latitude, is the **southernmost point** of the **Indian Union** and is situated on this island.
 
• The island is home to the **Shompen** tribe, who are hunter-gatherers and classified as a **Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Group (PVTG)**. They have lived in isolation in the interior forests for centuries.
 
• The **Galathea Bay** on **Great Nicobar** is one of the most significant **nesting sites** in the world for the **Giant Leatherback Turtle**, the largest of all living sea turtles.
